name: The Court of Wayreth: Stat Blocks

text.content:
Written for D&D 5e (2014). These are journal-format rather than Actor documents so they survive dnd5e system updates — drop them into your world and build Actors from them if you want tokens.

A Warning About Raistlin

His stat block exists so you know what happens if the party attacks him. It is not a boss fight and Shadow of the Dragon Queen tops out around 11th level, which is roughly half of what would be needed.

If the party attacks the Master of Wayreth in his own Tower, the honest answer is that they lose, immediately, and the interesting question is what he does with them afterward. He does not kill guests. He is much worse than that: he is disappointed, he has them shown out, and the forest does not admit them again.

Conclave Casters in General

Every Wizard of High Sorcery stat block here is subject to moon sanction (see Moons and Sanction). Roll their moon before any encounter. A Black Robe met in low sanction is a substantially different fight, and the party will never know why unless they work it out.

Medium humanoid (human), lawful evil — Challenge 21 (33,000 XP)

Armor Class 18 (mage armor, ring)
Hit Points 190 (28d8 + 64)
Speed 25 ft.

STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
7 (−2)14 (+2)10 (+0)24 (+7)18 (+4)16 (+3)

Saving Throws Int +14, Wis +11, Cha +10
Skills Arcana +21, History +14, Insight +11, Perception +11
Damage Resistances psychic; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks
Condition Immunities charmed, frightened
Senses truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 21
Languages Common, Elvish, Draconic, Abyssal, Solamnic, and the language of magic

Traits

The Hourglass Eyes. Raistlin sees all living things as they will be. He automatically knows the current hit points, conditions, and remaining lifespan of any creature he can see. He cannot be surprised, and he has disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks against living creatures — he cannot stop seeing them die.

Failing Body. At the start of each of his turns, roll a d20. On a 1, Raistlin is wracked by the cough: he cannot take reactions and cannot cast spells with verbal components until the end of his next turn. He does not attempt to conceal this.

Unsanctioned. Raistlin does not suffer low sanction and gains high sanction benefits regardless of the black moon's phase. No one has established why.

Master of the Tower. While inside Wayreth, Raistlin knows the location of every creature in the building, cannot be surprised or teleported against his will, and any creature that attacks him has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes each turn.

Legendary Resistance (3/Day). If he fails a saving throw, he may choose to succeed instead.

Spellcasting

20th-level wizard. Spell save DC 22, +14 to hit with spell attacks. He has the following prepared:

Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, mage hand, message, minor illusion, prestidigitation
1st (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, shield, silent image
2nd (3): hold person, invisibility, mirror image, suggestion
3rd (3): counterspell, dispel magic, fireball, fly
4th (3): banishment, dimension door, greater invisibility, phantasmal killer
5th (3): bigby's hand, scrying, wall of force
6th (2): chain lightning, globe of invulnerability, true seeing
7th (2): forcecage, plane shift, teleport
8th (1): maze, mind blank
9th (1): time stop

Actions

Staff of Magius. Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) force damage.

Legendary Actions (3/round)

Cantrip. Cast a cantrip.
Withdraw (Costs 2). Teleport up to 60 feet to a space he can see.
Observe (Costs 2). One creature Raistlin can see makes a DC 22 Wisdom save or takes 18 (4d8) psychic damage and has disadvantage on its next attack roll. On a success, half damage. He does not appear to do anything.

DM Note

Time stop is on the list for a reason. If he ever needs to end an encounter, he stops time, walks to the door, and resumes it from the other side of it. He does not fight people he has already beaten.

Par-Salian of the White Robes

Medium humanoid (human), lawful neutral — Challenge 15 (13,000 XP)

AC 15 (mage armor) • HP 135 (18d8 + 54) • Speed 30 ft.

STR 9 (−1) • DEX 14 (+2) • CON 16 (+3) • INT 21 (+5) • WIS 18 (+4) • CHA 15 (+2)

Saves Int +11, Wis +10 • Skills Arcana +16, History +11, Insight +10 • Senses passive Perception 14 • Languages Common, Elvish, Solamnic, Draconic

Head of the Conclave. Once per long rest, Par-Salian may declare the Conclave's writ. Every creature of his choosing within 60 feet that is a Wizard of High Sorcery must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma save or be unable to cast spells against him for one minute.

Spellcasting. 17th-level wizard, save DC 19, +11 to hit. Notable: counterspell, dispel magic, banishment, wall of force, scrying, true seeing, forcecage, antimagic field, foresight.

Roleplay: he does not want to fight anyone and will spend the first three rounds of any combat trying to end it. He is very good at ending them.

Ladonna of the Black Robes

Medium humanoid (human), neutral evil — Challenge 14 (11,500 XP)

AC 16 • HP 120 (16d8 + 48) • Speed 30 ft.

STR 10 (+0) • DEX 16 (+3) • CON 16 (+3) • INT 20 (+5) • WIS 15 (+2) • CHA 18 (+4)

Saves Int +10, Cha +9 • Skills Arcana +15, Deception +14, Insight +7 • Languages Common, Abyssal, Draconic, Thieves' Cant

Perfectly Frank. Ladonna has advantage on Charisma checks made when she is telling the complete truth about her own motives, which is most of the time and is far more disarming than lying.

Spellcasting. 16th-level wizard, save DC 18, +10 to hit. Notable: hold person, suggestion, fear, greater invisibility, dominate person, contact other plane, finger of death, feeblemind.

Justarius of the Red Robes

Medium humanoid (human), neutral — Challenge 13 (10,000 XP)

AC 15 • HP 110 (15d8 + 45) • Speed 20 ft. (lame in the left leg, a price from his own Test)

STR 11 (+0) • DEX 12 (+1) • CON 17 (+3) • INT 20 (+5) • WIS 16 (+3) • CHA 17 (+3)

Saves Int +10, Wis +8 • Skills Arcana +15, Insight +8, Persuasion +8 • Languages Common, Elvish, Draconic, Dwarvish

The Balance. When a creature within 30 feet casts a spell, Justarius may use his reaction to grant that spell advantage or impose disadvantage on its first attack roll or saving throw. He decides after seeing the target.

Spellcasting. 15th-level wizard, save DC 18, +10 to hit. Notable: shield, misty step, counterspell, fire shield, telekinesis, chain lightning, reverse gravity.

Dalamar Argent

Medium humanoid (elf), neutral evil — Challenge 8 (3,900 XP)

AC 14 • HP 78 (12d8 + 24) • Speed 30 ft.

STR 9 (−1) • DEX 15 (+2) • CON 14 (+2) • INT 18 (+4) • WIS 14 (+2) • CHA 16 (+3)

Saves Int +8, Wis +6 • Skills Arcana +12, Deception +11, Stealth +6 • Senses darkvision 60 ft. • Languages Common, Elvish, Draconic

Two Masters. Dalamar has advantage on saves against effects that would compel him to reveal information, and on Deception checks made to conceal his loyalties. He is not sure himself which way he would jump.

Spellcasting. 12th-level wizard, save DC 16, +8 to hit. Notable: charm person, invisibility, counterspell, fear, greater invisibility, dominate person, disintegrate.

Guardian of the Tower

Medium undead, lawful neutral — Challenge 12 (8,400 XP)

The Orders' oldest and least discussed practice. When a Wizard of High Sorcery of sufficient devotion dies, they may petition to remain — and the ones who are accepted stand in the Tower's corridors for as long as it stands. They are not animated corpses. They are volunteers, and they remember being people.

AC 18 (natural) • HP 149 (18d8 + 68) • Speed 30 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover)

STR 18 (+4) • DEX 14 (+2) • CON 18 (+4) • INT 16 (+3) • WIS 18 (+4) • CHA 15 (+2)

Saves Con +9, Wis +9 • Damage Immunities cold, necrotic, poison; nonmagical weapons • Condition Immunities charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned • Senses truesight 60 ft.

Bound to the Stone. A Guardian cannot leave Wayreth and cannot be permanently destroyed within it — reduced to 0 hit points, it reforms at the door it was set to guard after 24 hours. It is fully aware of this and it makes them very calm.

Duty. A Guardian attacks only creatures violating the Tower's rules of conduct, and stops the instant the violation stops. It will accept a surrender. It will explain the rules first, in a voice that is politely apologetic.

Actions. Multiattack: two Chill Touch attacks. Chill Touch: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) necrotic, and the target's hit point maximum is reduced by the damage until it finishes a long rest.

Gaze of the Departed (Recharge 5–6): One creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 17 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is frightened for one minute and sees, clearly, the moment of its own death. It may repeat the save at the end of each turn.

Renegade Hunter

Medium humanoid (any race), any alignment — Challenge 9 (5,000 XP)

Dispatched by the Conclave against unlicensed casters. Competent, patient, and authorised.

AC 16 (studded leather, shield) • HP 91 (14d8 + 28) • Speed 30 ft.

STR 12 (+1) • DEX 18 (+4) • CON 14 (+2) • INT 17 (+3) • WIS 15 (+2) • CHA 12 (+1)

Saves Dex +8, Int +7 • Skills Arcana +11, Investigation +11, Perception +6, Stealth +8

Writ of the Conclave. The hunter has advantage on attack rolls and saving throws against any creature it has formally declared renegade. It always declares first. It considers this a matter of professional pride.

Counterspelling Reflex. The hunter may cast counterspell twice per long rest without expending a slot.

Spellcasting. 9th-level wizard, save DC 15, +7 to hit. Notable: shield, silvery barbs, misty step, counterspell, hypnotic pattern, dimension door, hold monster.

Actions. Multiattack: two Shortsword attacks. Shortsword: +8 to hit, Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing plus 10 (3d6) force against a creature that has cast a spell since the hunter's last turn.

Hunter's Rod (3/day): As described in The Vaults. DC 16.

DM Note — Hunters as Antagonists

Renegade hunters are the best recurring antagonist in this supplement precisely because they are right. They are enforcing a law that exists for a coherent reason, they will negotiate, and they will stop if the target agrees to take the Test.

If a PC refuses the Test, send one. Not to kill them — to talk, first, at length, and to be entirely reasonable about it. Then send the same one again three sessions later, less patient.
